title: Hikmat al-Ishraq (Arabic-Persian, Delhi 1920 print)
author: Shihab al-Din Suhrawardi
description: Hikmat al-Ishraq (The Philosophy of Illumination) by Shihab al-Din Yahya Suhrawardi (1154-1191), here in an Arabic printing with Persian material (Delhi, 1920), probably with commentary. Suhrawardi, executed in Aleppo at the age of thirty-eight and known as Shaykh al-Ishraq, founded the Illuminationist school of Islamic philosophy. In this masterwork he criticises aspects of Aristotelian logic and metaphysics as taught by Avicenna and develops a metaphysics of light: all reality is a hierarchy of lights emanating from the Light of Lights, with knowledge as presence and self-illumination. He integrates Platonic Forms as angelic 'lords of the species', ancient Persian wisdom (the xvarnah or royal glory and Zoroastrian angelology) and Hermetic themes, and describes an intermediate 'world of images' (alam al-mithal). It profoundly shaped later Persian philosophy, including Mulla Sadra.
